organizations.normalization_notes: The OSS interview says only 'Red Cross'. Do not silently normalize to American Red Cross or another national society without a direct record.

affiliations.date_precision: The May 1944 interview says Dinga came to OSS in March 'this year' from the Red Cross; OCR suggests a day but the exact day is not asserted.
affiliations.research_notes: Direct wartime OSS interview names Martin Dinga, labels him a civilian, places his Red Cross work before OSS, and distinguishes still earlier New York social work. Exact Red Cross society and job title remain unspecified; paid-role interpretation is supported by the interview's later question on what he received there.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Eugene A Dinet Jr. has a high-confidence match to a Harvard Law Bulletin OSS service notice.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Harvard's class note gives the full name and suffix, states wartime OSS service, and dates his law-school class after the war.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Distinctive full name, initial, suffix, and explicit OSS association agree with the index; no serial comparison is available from this source.
claims.temporal_assessment: The bulletin documents OSS service and later teaching, not a pre-OSS employer.
claims.match_notes: Do not backdate postwar teaching to pre-OSS employment. A 1909 Eugene A Dinet in Wisconsin directories is a different generation or unproven namesake.

claims.claim_text: A wartime OSS interview identifies Martin Dinga as a civilian serving at the Slovak desk.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The interview names Martin Dinga, labels him civilian, and describes his OSS work and prior Red Cross connection.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The uncommon full name and direct wartime OSS context support a high-confidence match to the indexed Martin Dinga; the transcript lacks a box or serial identifier.
claims.temporal_assessment: Wartime OSS identity and explicit prior affiliation are recorded together.
claims.match_notes: Preserve the index's blank rank field; the interview supports civilian status only.

claims.claim_text: Martin Dinga was with the Red Cross immediately before joining the OSS in Cairo in 1944.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Asked where he was recruited, Dinga said he had been with the Red Cross; a follow-up contrasts that period with earlier social work.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Direct named OSS interview, with uncommon indexed full name and matching wartime context.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate predecessor to OSS. The source does not specify which national Red Cross society or a precise job title.
claims.match_notes: Use source wording 'Red Cross'; do not silently expand to American Red Cross.

sources.locator_override: Interview LVI, printed p. 62, PDF p. 65

claims.claim_text: The Red Cross is Dinga's last documented civilian employer before OSS service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The interview calls Dinga a civilian, identifies his Red Cross position as the role before OSS, and discusses what he received there.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Direct contemporaneous named OSS interview; same high-confidence identity assessment as the immediate-affiliation claim.
claims.temporal_assessment: Red Cross directly precedes civilian OSS employment; older New York social work precedes the Red Cross but no employer is named.
claims.match_notes: Employment rather than volunteer status is supported by the interview's compensation comparison, but precise title and national society are unknown.

sources.locator_override: Interview LVI, printed pp. 62-63, PDF pp. 65-66

claims.claim_text: Before the Red Cross, Dinga performed social work connected with children's aid and settlement houses in New York City; no employer is named.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The interviewer asks what preceded the Red Cross and Dinga describes social work in New York City without identifying a particular employer.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Same direct named OSS interview and high-confidence indexed-person match.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly earlier than the Red Cross and thus earlier than OSS, but the organizations and dates are unspecified.
claims.match_notes: Occupation only. Do not normalize generic children's aid or settlement houses to any specific New York institution.
